headline: Generative and predictive models span DNA, enzyme, metabolic and single-cell data
label: Generative Biomolecular Design Models
summary: Unified benchmarks and topology- and alignment-aware encodings are now appearing across enzymatic, genomic and single-cell modeling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is representation design that encodes biomolecular structure directly into model inputs or objectives. STAMP encodes fragment motifs, attachment sites and tree topology in a molecular language to support fragment-level learning and editing, while USM-AA adds alignment-aware rotary positional encoding with chromosome, strand and CIGAR embeddings for long-range DNA modeling. BioMod replaces genes with 660 overlapping biological modules as tokens in a 50M-parameter single-cell model. On the function side, VenusRX-Bench and VenusRX unify enzymatic reaction prediction, retrosynthesis and EC prediction, GMSF fuses atom-atom mapping difference graphs with multiscale sequence encoding, and MPA-EC uses a generative LLM to infer microenvironment before EC reasoning. QuotientPO differs in targeting metabolic model repair through quotient-space exploration. What is new is the convergence of generation, prediction and shared evaluation across these modalities.
